text:
Apple reports fourth quarter results - Apple

# Apple reports fourth quarter results 

 September quarter records for total company revenue, iPhone revenue, and EPS Services revenue reaches new all-time high 

CUPERTINO, CALIFORNIA Apple today announced financial results for its fiscal 2026 fourth quarter ended September 26, 2026. The Company posted quarterly revenue of $114.5 billion, up 12 percent year over year. Company gross margin was 47.9 percent, including a favorable impact of approximately 1 percentage point from tariff refunds. Diluted earnings per share was $2.10, up 14 percent year over year, and included a favorable impact of $0.05 from tariff refunds. 

“Today, Apple is proud to report a September quarter revenue record of $114.5 billion, up 12 percent from a year ago, with iPhone reaching a September quarter record and Services reaching an all-time high, capping off our best fiscal year ever,” said John Ternus, Apple’s CEO. “We’re closing the year with our most ambitious lineup yet. That includes the iPhone Duo, the most transformational iPhone since the original, alongside iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max, our most powerful iPhones yet. We also just introduced a whole new generation of hardware for the home and brought Touch to Mac for the first time. Together with the all-new Siri AI, it’s an incredible lineup to carry us into the holiday season.” 

“Apple delivered September quarter records for net income and EPS. Our record September quarter capped off a strong fiscal 2026, with all-time record revenue of $479 billion and double-digit EPS growth,” said Kevan Parekh, Apple’s CFO. “We generated $28 billion in operating cash flow during the quarter, allowing us to return $28 billion to shareholders. Thanks to our very high levels of customer satisfaction and loyalty, our installed base of active devices reached a new all-time high across all major product categories and geographic segments.” 

Apple’s board of directors has declared a cash dividend of $0.27 per share of the Company’s common stock. The dividend is payable on November 16, 2026, to shareholders of record as of the close of business on November 12, 2026. 

Apple will provide live streaming of its Q4 2026 financial results conference call beginning at 2:00 p.m. PT on November 2, 2026, at apple.com/investor/earnings-call. The webcast will be available for replay for approximately two weeks thereafter. 

- Consolidated Financial Statements

 View PDF 

### About Apple 

Apple revolutionized personal technology with the introduction of the Macintosh in 1984. Today, Apple leads the world in innovation with iPhone, iPad, Mac, AirPods, Apple Watch, and Apple Vision Pro. Apple’s six software platforms — iOS, iPadOS, macOS, watchOS, visionOS, and tvOS — provide seamless experiences across all Apple devices and empower people with breakthrough services including the App Store, Apple Music, Apple Pay, iCloud, and Apple TV. Apple’s more than 150,000 employees are dedicated to making the best products on earth and to leaving the world better than we found it.

Apple earnings Q4: $114.5B, $2.10 EPS | RR Tech Pulse

# Apple earnings Q4: $114.5B revenue, $2.10 EPS, record Services

September-quarter revenue reached $114.5 billion, up 12 percent, with diluted EPS of $2.10 and gross margin of 47.9 percent. The company also declared a $0.27 dividend.

By Ramiz Raja · Published Nov 2, 2026, 4:45 PM EST · Updated Nov 2, 2026, 7:14 PM EST

Update: Revision 3: added December-quarter guidance from the Nov. 2 earnings call.

Apple Park in Cupertino. Image: Apple

In its fiscal fourth-quarter results, Apple posted revenue of $114.5 billion for the quarter ended Sept. 26, 2026, up 12 percent from a year earlier. Diluted earnings per share were $2.10, up 14 percent. Apple's release calls these September quarter records for total company revenue, iPhone revenue and EPS, and says Services revenue reached a new all-time high.

Updated with segment revenue from Apple's financial statements.

Update, Nov. 2 (after the call, ET): On the earnings call, CFO Kevan Parekh said Apple expects December-quarter total company revenue to grow between 7% and 10% year over year, which he said "reflects our best view of constrained supply." He also guided gross margin to between 45% and 46% and Services revenue growth to between 8% and 9%. He said the guidance "assumes that global tariff rates, policies, and their application remain in effect as of this call, and the global macroeconomic outlook does not worsen from today," per the call transcript from Six Colors.

## What changed

This is Apple's earnings report for the September quarter. Apple's release gives these figures:

| Measure | Apple's figure |
| --- | --- |
| Quarterly revenue | $114.5 billion, up 12 percent year over year |
| Diluted EPS | $2.10, up 14 percent year over year |
| Company gross margin | 47.9 percent |
| Operating cash flow | $28 billion |
| Returned to shareholders | $28 billion |
| Fiscal 2026 revenue | $479 billion, an all-time record |
| Dividend | $0.27 per share |

Apple says gross margin includes a favorable impact of about 1 percentage point from tariff refunds, and that diluted EPS includes a favorable $0.05 from tariff refunds. In other words, part of the margin and earnings figures came from refunds rather than from selling more hardware.

Apple's consolidated financial statements fill in the detail the release text leaves out. iPhone was the largest category at $57.6 billion, up 17.5 percent from $49.0 billion a year earlier. Services reached $31.6 billion, up 9.8 percent from $28.8 billion. Mac rose 23.7 percent to $10.8 billion. iPad and Wearables, Home and Accessories both fell from the year-ago quarter.

| Category (US$ millions) | Q4 FY2026 | Q4 FY2025 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| iPhone | 57,583 | 49,025 |
| Mac | 10,792 | 8,726 |
| iPad | 6,229 | 6,952 |
| Wearables, Home and Accessories | 8,300 | 9,013 |
| Services | 31,573 | 28,750 |
| Total net sales | 114,477 | 102,466 |

By region, Greater China grew fastest, up 21.0 percent to $17.5 billion. Japan was the only reportable segment that declined, slipping from $6,636 million to $6,540 million.

| Segment (US$ millions) | Q4 FY2026 | Q4 FY2025 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Americas | 48,680 | 44,192 |
| Europe | 32,008 | 28,703 |
| Greater China | 17,539 | 14,493 |
| Japan | 6,540 | 6,636 |
| Rest of Asia Pacific | 9,710 | 8,442 |
| Total net sales | 114,477 | 102,466 |

CFO Kevan Parekh is quoted saying Apple delivered September quarter records for net income and EPS, and that the installed base of active devices reached a new all-time high across all major product categories and geographic segments. The financial statements put net income at $30,711 million, compared with $27,466 million a year earlier.

The dividend is payable Nov. 16, 2026, to shareholders of record as of the close of business on Nov. 12, 2026.

## Who is affected

Apple's release also mentions its fall hardware lineup. For background on those products, see our report on what Apple announced at its Welcome Home event and the iPhone Duo pre-order and price story. It names the iPhone Duo, iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, new home hardware and Touch on Mac in that lineup. It does not give sales numbers for any of them.

Earlier reporting that Apple may have trimmed component orders for the iPhone 18 Pro, covered in our production-cut report, came from a third party. Apple's release does not mention component orders or production, so these results neither confirm nor refute that report.

## What this means for you

If you are deciding whether to buy an iPhone, the release does not change prices, stock or trade-in values, and it says nothing about shipping times. A record September quarter for iPhone revenue means iPhone brought in more than in any earlier September quarter; it does not say how many phones were sold, since the release gives no unit counts.

If you follow Apple as an investor, the headline margin and EPS include a benefit from tariff refunds, which Apple itself separates out. R

title: Apple's ad business sets all-time record as Services gains 10% to $31.6bn
author: Luis Rijo
text:
Apple's ad business sets all-time record as Services gains 10% to $31.6bn

Apple’s ads set an all-time record inside a $31.6bn Services line, but Apple won’t say how big

# Apple's ad business sets all-time record as Services gains 10% to $31.6bn

Services earned $24bn of Apple's $54.8bn gross profit as Maps ads reached US and Canadian firms. How far can ads carry growth that Apple now guides to 8-9%?

- by Luis Rijo

Luis Rijo

Luís Rijo has written PPC Land daily since founding it in 2016. Over 10,000 articles, funded by readers, no sponsored coverage. Tips and corrections: luis@ppc.land

- LinkedIn 
- November 3, 2026
- •
- 16 min read

Apple's advertising business set an all-time revenue record in the three months to September 26, 2026, chief financial officer Kevan Parekh told analysts on November 2, the day Apple reported that Services revenue rose 10% to $31.573 billion. Apple again published no advertising figure. Its results release does not mention advertising, and the condensed financial statements fold ads into a single Services line alongside the App Store, iCloud, Apple Pay, AppleCare, music and video. What the numbers do show is a Services business that slowed from 16% growth in the March quarter to 12% in June and 10% in September, while producing 43.7% of Apple's gross profit from 27.6% of its revenue. For the December quarter, Apple guided Services growth to between 8% and 9%, and named third-party licensing as one of the main drags - a category that Apple's own annual report counts as part of advertising.

## In Short

Apple made $31.6 billion between July and September from services such as the App Store, iCloud and advertising, 10% more than a year earlier, and its finance chief said the ad business had its best quarter ever, although Apple still does not say how much money ads bring in. That matters to app developers and local businesses that buy Apple's ads in the App Store and, since August, in Apple Maps, because it shows Apple's ad unit growing while the rest of Services slows. Apple expects Services growth to drop again to 8% or 9% in the last three months of 2026, partly because of licensing deals that Apple's annual report files under advertising.

## What Apple filed on November 2

Apple published three documents on November 2, 2026: a press release headed "Apple reports fourth quarter results," a set of condensed consolidated financial statements, and a Form 8-K that furnishes the release to the Securities and Exchange Commission under Item 2.02. The 8-K is signed by Parekh as senior vice president and chief financial officer. All three cover the fiscal fourth quarter ended September 26, 2026, which closed Apple's fiscal year.

Revenue for the quarter was $114.477 billion, up from $102.466 billion a year earlier. Apple rounds that to 12%; the exact figure is 11.7%. Gross margin was 47.9%, which the release says included "a favorable impact of approximately 1 percentage point from tariff refunds." Diluted earnings per share were $2.10, up 14%, including $0.05 from the same refunds. Net income reached $30.711 billion.

Chief executive John Ternus, presenting results for the first time since taking over from Tim Cook, described the quarter in the release as "a September quarter revenue record of $114.5 billion, up 12 percent from a year ago, with iPhone reaching a September quarter record and Services reaching an all-time high, capping off our best fiscal year ever." Parekh added that the quarter "capped off a strong fiscal 2026, with all-time record revenue of $479 billion and double-digit EPS growth."

Neither quote mentions advertising. Nor does any other sentence in the release. The boilerplate at the bottom lists "the App Store, Apple Music, Apple Pay, iCloud, and Apple TV" as examples of Apple's services. The financial statements split revenue into Products and Services, and Products into iPhone, Mac, iPad, and Wearables, Home and Accessories. There is no advertising row, no App Store row and no licensing row. Everything this article says about Apple's advertising performance in the quarter comes from Parekh's remarks on the conference call, held at 2:00 p.m. Pacific time on November 2, and from Apple's earlier filings.

## The Services line, quarter by quarter

The Services line is the only place in Apple's accounts where advertising lives, so its arithmetic sets the outer limit of what can be said about ads.

| Three months ended | Sept 26, 2026 | Sept 27, 2025 | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Services revenue | $31.573bn | $28.750bn | +9.8% |
| Cost of Services | $7.593bn | $7.106bn | +6.9% |
| Services gross profit | $23.980bn | $21.644bn | +10.8% |
| Services gross margin | 76.0% | 75.3% | +0.7 points |
| Services share of revenue | 27.6% | 28.1% | -0.5 points |
| Services share of gross profit | 43.7% | 44.8% | -1.0 points |

Apple's regional segments - Americas, Europe, Greater China, Japan and Rest of Asia Pacific - combine hardware and services, and the release gives no Services figure for any region.

The products that create Apple's ad audience grew unevenly. iPhone revenue rose 17.5% to $57.583 billion, a September-quarter record. Mac revenue rose 23.7% to $10.792 billion. iPad fell 10.4% to $6.229 billion, and Wearables, Home and Accessories fell 7.9% to $8.300 billion.

By segment, Greater China grew fastest at 21.0%, to $17.539 billion. Europe rose 11.5% to $32.008 billion, the Americas 10.2% to $48.680 billion, and Rest of Asia Pacific 15.0% to $9.710 billion. Japan fell 1.4% to $6.540 billion.

author: Dhan
text:
Apple Q4FY26 results: iPhone sales hit $57.52B, EPS up 14%

# Apple Q4FY26 results: iPhone sales hit $57.52B, EPS up 14% 

 5 min read | Published on 03 Nov 2026, 03:12 AM | Updated on 03 Nov 2026, 05:45 AM 

Reviewed by

Naman S ScanX News Team

Key Highlights

- Total Q4FY26 revenue reached $114.477 billion, beating estimates
- Mac revenue surged to $10.792 billion from $8.726 billion YoY
- iPhone sales hit $57.5183 billion, driving product segment growth
- Services revenue expanded to $31.57 billion, an all-time high

*this image is generated using AI for illustrative purposes only.

 Apple Inc reported fourth-quarter fiscal 2026 revenue of $114.477 billion, beating analyst estimates of $113.392 billion. Earnings per share rose 13.51% year-over-year to $2.10, surpassing consensus of $1.98.

The Cupertino-based company capped off its best fiscal year ever, with total annual revenue reaching a record $479 billion. This marks the first earnings call under new CEO John Ternus, who highlighted the launch of the all-new iPhone Duo and the introduction of Siri AI as pivotal moments for the company. Ternus stated that Siri AI marks a new chapter in AI at Apple, noting it is built on a modern orchestrator-driven architecture designed for privacy. He also confirmed that Apple's India business hit record revenue in the fourth quarter.

## Margin dynamics and cost pressures

During the earnings call, CFO Kevan Parekh addressed the factors influencing profitability. He noted that gross margins would have been down without tariff refunds. These refunds played a critical role in mitigating the impact of high memory costs, allowing the company to maintain its margin profile despite rising component prices. Parekh further clarified that higher memory costs and ongoing Siri AI development expenses will continue to affect gross margins going forward. Specifically, Parekh stated that Apple sees pricing for memory purchases continuing to increase, signaling sustained pressure on input costs.

Looking ahead to the December quarter (Q1FY27), management guided for gross margins between 45% and 46%, down from 47.9% in Q4FY26. Parekh attributed this sequential decline primarily to higher memory costs and costs related to the ramp of Siri AI. The CFO noted that while tariff refunds provided a ~1 percentage point benefit in Q4FY26, the vast majority of these refunds have now been received, removing this tailwind for future quarters.

## Supply chain commitments

Parekh disclosed that Apple's manufacturing purchase obligations increased by $33 billion between the June and September quarters. This significant rise in committed spending underscores the scale of production planning required to meet demand across its hardware portfolio. Sabih Khan, Senior Vice President of Operations, added that supply constraints on iPhone, Mac, and iPad in Q4FY26 were driven by high demand and limited availability of advanced nodes. For the December quarter, constraints are expected to persist on Mac and iPad, primarily driven by memory availability.

## Regional performance breakdown

The Americas remained the largest contributor with $48.680 billion in regional revenue for the September quarter. Europe followed with $32.008 billion. Greater China recorded $17.539 billion, while Japan and Rest of Asia Pacific posted $6.540 billion and $9.71 billion respectively. The disclosure of record revenue for India adds a key growth driver to the Asia-Pacific segment, though specific figures were not broken out separately from the broader regional totals.

| Region | Revenue | Context |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Americas | $48.680 billion | Largest contributor |
| Europe | $32.008 billion | Second largest |
| Greater China | $17.539 billion | Key Asian market |
| Rest of Asia Pacific | $9.71 billion | Other APAC markets |
| Japan | $6.540 billion | Smallest listed segment |

## Product and services growth

Product revenue grew to $82.90 billion from $73.72 billion in the prior year period. Services revenue expanded to $31.57 billion from $28.75 billion. The breakdown by category shows strong momentum in core hardware, although iPad sales faced headwinds:

- iPhone: $57.5183 billion (up from $49.025 billion). New models include the foldable iPhone Duo and iPhone 18 Pro.
- Mac: $10.792 billion (up from $8.726 billion). Growth driven by MacBook Neo and MacBook Pro, despite supply constraints.
- iPad: $6.229 billion (down 10% YoY). Decline attributed to supply constraints and a difficult comparison against the prior year's launch of $6.952 billion.
- Wearables, Home and Accessories: $8.3 billion (down from $9.013 billion YoY). Impacted by tough comps against Watch SE3 and AirPods Pro 3 launches.

# AAPL (AAPL) Q4 FY2026 Earnings Recap

Nov 2, 2026

AAPL (AAPL) reported Q4 FY2026 earnings on November 2, 2026. The company posted revenue of $114.5B (+12% YoY) and GAAP EPS of $2.10 (+14% YoY).

## Key Metrics

| Metric | Value | YoY Change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Revenue | $114.5B | +12% |
| GAAP EPS | $2.10 | +14% |
| Gross Margin | 47.9% | — |
| Net Income | $30.7B | +12% |

## Segment Breakdown

| Segment | Revenue | YoY | % of Total |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| iPhone | $57.6B | +17% | 50% |
| Services | $31.6B | +10% | 28% |
| Mac | $10.8B | +24% | 9% |
| Wearables, Home and Accessories | $8.3B | -8% | 7% |
| iPad | $6.2B | -10% | 5% |

## Full-Year Summary (FY2026)

| Metric | Value | Change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Total Revenue | $478.8B | +15% YoY |
| Net Income | $132.2B | +18% YoY |
| Diluted EPS | $8.98 | +20% YoY |
| Gross Margin | $233.6B | +20% YoY |
| Operating Cash Flow | $145.1B | +30% YoY |
| R&D Expense | $45.8B | +32% YoY |
| Shareholder Returns (Dividends + Buybacks) | $102.1B | null |

## Key Highlights

- September quarter revenue record of $114.5B, up 12% YoY, with all-time record fiscal year revenue of $478.8B
- iPhone revenue reached a September quarter record of $57.6B, up 17% YoY
- Services revenue hit a new all-time high of $31.6B, up 10% YoY
- Gross margin of 47.9% included ~1 percentage point favorable impact from tariff refunds ($0.05 EPS benefit)
- Installed base of active devices reached all-time highs across all major product categories and geographic segments

## Risks & Headwinds

Gross margin benefited from approximately 1 percentage point of tariff refunds, which may not recur; iPad and Wearables/Home/Accessories segments declined YoY; R&D spending surged 32% YoY suggesting heavy investment cycle; inventories nearly tripled YoY to $14.5B; ongoing risks from trade disputes, geopolitical tensions, and complex regulatory environments, particularly in Greater China.

## CEO Commentary

> "Today, Apple is proud to report a September quarter revenue record of $114.5 billion, up 12 percent from a year ago, with iPhone reaching a September quarter record and Services reaching an all-time high, capping off our best fiscal year ever. We're closing the year with our most ambitious lineup yet." — John Ternus, CEO
